articles.title: Are baby products the secret to better skin? 15 toiletries worth trying
articles.summary: With gentler formulas and lower prices, children’s toiletries can work just as well for adults. From nappy rash cream to nourishing bath milk, these are the products that have earned a place in my routine.
body: There may be plenty of worrying headlines about children using adult beauty products from younger and younger ages, but what about the reverse?

I’ve been a beauty editor for more than a decade, but when I had my first child in 2020, I was immediately impressed with the body washes, bath products and moisturisers designed for babies, particularly as someone with eczema and sensitive skin. The products’ gentler, often fragrance-free formulas are easier on my skin, tend to cost less, and result in a less cluttered bathroom, since we can all use the same things. These are the ones I’m still using – on the entire family – five years on.

This was the only nappy cream I ever used on my children as babies, since it seemed to clear up any hint of a rash before it got bad. But it also works miracles when dabbed on my and my son’s eczema flare-ups (calendula is anti-inflammatory). The lanolin ingredient creates a barrier to lock in moisture, and the calendula and chamomile bring down redness quickly and effectively. It leaves a white cast, though, so avoid using it on your face.
points: With gentler formulas and lower prices, children’s toiletries can work just as well for adults.

articles.title: ‘If you’re just interested in answers, you are missing out’: philosopher Lani Watson on the power of asking questions
articles.summary: The author and academic explains how an open, questioning mindset can bring people with opposing views closer together – and even change history. Asking a question can change your mood, and having a questioning mindset can change your life – or, as the philosopher Lani Watson, an honorary fellow at…
body: Questioning fosters exploration and curiosity, she says. It changes your relationship to yourself and to others: it can make you fall in love; it can stop you going to war. Watson’s challenging book, Q: The Hidden Power of Questions in a World that Wants Answers, is written with a deceptive simplicity and an almost kindly encouragement, so you’re knee-deep into her proposition before you have even considered that it might turn out to be quite hard work.

The book is unusually interactive, asking the reader to read a sentence out loud, count the number of questions in a conversation between Watson and her wife, ask basic questions of themselves and stop to think about whether they can be answered. There’s an appendix at the end that promises to get you into a questioning frame of mind, which it turns out you have to write yourself (to be fair, there’s no trickery here; she does say that it’s empty – but in my reflexive quest for answers, I didn’t notice).
points: The author and academic explains how an open, questioning mindset can bring people with opposing views closer together – and even change history.

articles.title: Jimi Famurewa’s leek, bacon and focaccia breakfast bake – recipe
articles.summary: New Guardian Food show FEED with Jimi Famurewa travels the UK in search of food trends. This dish combines the best of Welsh nostalgia with a modern twist. The main inspiration for this dish is the Swansea breakfast at Bara, a much-hyped and nationally famous Welsh-inspired cafe in Peckham, south…
body: The way that an unusual mix of cockles, bacon, leeks, eggs and laverbread has been embraced by a cool crowd shows that nostalgic British and Irish dishes are being reinvented and reappraised for a new generation by creative young chefs up and down the land.

There isn’t laverbread in this recipe, but the dijon mustard, combined with the oven-baked eggs that create a kind of savoury bread pudding/Cambrian French toast hybrid, provides similar oomph and moreishness – perfect with the sweet flavour of the Sainsbury’s Taste the Difference baby leeks.

Heat your oven to 200C (180C fan)/390F/gas 6. Tear the focaccia into large bite-size pieces and spread out in a baking dish. Put into the oven for 3-4 minutes or until the bread has dried out. Then remove from the oven and set aside, leaving the bread in the dish.
Meanwhile, cook the bacon according to packet instructions. Let it cool slightly before roughly chopping into small pieces.

articles.title: Why dodgy doors are the latest casualty of the UK heatwaves
articles.summary: Sticking or unlockable doors are yet another problem caused by the hot summer, but winter can also bring difficulties. Thursday was another busy day for Alan Hickman, a Bournemouth-based locksmith who works in the area around the New Forest (“though I’m currently dodging the bit between Ringwood…
body: Speaking on his way to see a man who can’t close his patio doors – “probably because they’ve got some expansion issues” – he then has a callout to see an elderly woman who needs a lockbox installed for her carer, before visiting a customer in Westbourne “to sort another composite door that can’t lock”.

Such cases of sticking, unopenable or unlockable doors are much more common at the moment, says Hickman, due, like so much else, to the very hot weather across much of the UK over the past few months.

“We’re getting what feels like double the amount of calls a day because customers’ doors just aren’t able to open, or they can’t close them at the end of a hot day until they’ve cooled down again,” he says. Hickman has worked with LockRite, one of the UK’s largest networks of uniformed locksmiths, for 14 years but this summer has “definitely brought a significant increase” in heat-related callouts.

articles.title: Jacob Elordi Doesn’t Mind Being Mogged by His Co-Star, Rak the Dog
articles.summary: Oh, to be a Dogue, posing alongside Jacob Elordi—the co-stars appeared together on the red carpet for the world premiere of Ridley Scott’s “The Dog Stars.”
body: Elordi himself opted to wear Bottega Veneta, sporting a navy, softly pinstriped double-breasted suit with sharp lapels and coordinating tailored pants, a white shirt, and navy skinny tie. He wore diamond stud earrings, and his mini-mullet curly and tousled. He’s also been dutifully growing his returning mustache.

Rak and Elordi were also joined by the rest of the cast from The Dog Stars: Margaret Qualley, for one, chose to brave it in the freaky-deaky barefoot sandal that designer Matthieu Blazy presented during his r esort 2027 collection for Chanel in Biarritz, France, paired with a more classic and delicately fringed black dress. Dogs were out—figuratively and literally.

Off the red carpet, Elordi has been enjoying his time in London with rumored girlfriend Kendall Jenner. The pair were spotted out for a midweek meal with Jacob’s father at celebrity favorite Italian spot Cipriani. Both kept to their characteristically understated style, mirroring each other in elevated basics. Both Jacob Elordi and Kendall Jenner are known for keeping their private lives hush-hush, so it’s unlikely we’ll get a red carpet moment from the couple just yet.

body: It’s already begun: Dua Lipa has started her birthday celebrations early, kicking things off with some yacht shenanigans avec her siblings Rina and Gjin off the coast of Formentera.
The Lipa clan were photographed enjoying the blue Balearic waters yesterday, taking turns jumping into the sea and posing for the camera.

The pop star kept it Gucci in a leopard print bikini and matching crepe skirt, paired with thong sandals, oversized shades, and a cherry red Chanel shoulder bag. articles.title: The GLP-1 Pill Era Is Forcing Beauty to Change Again
articles.summary: GLP-1s have already upended the beauty market, creating a whole new host of skin and haircare concerns. Now, as GLP-1 pills reduce the barrier to entry, there’s more beauty innovation abound.
body: The UK has approved two GLP-1 tablets for weight management: Novo Nordisk’s Wegovy semaglutide tablet in June, and Eli Lilly’s Foundayo in August. Beyond removing the psychological and practical barrier of injections, oral formulations are not reliant on syringes or refrigeration and are cheaper to manufacture. In the US, oral Wegovy passed three million prescriptions within just over five months of launch, with the majority coming from people new to GLP-1 therapy. Mintel principal strategist Andrew McDougall says 22% of consumers would consider using GLP-1s in the future based on the approval of oral formats.
In the US, oral Wegovy passed three million prescriptions within just over five months of launch.

Dr. Jennifer Owens, an aesthetic practitioner from Reborne Longevity, a preventative health and longevity clinic in London’s Marylebone, expects the patient profile to broaden “dramatically”, from a relatively narrow cohort of committed, often clinically supervised injectable users to a “much larger, more casual, self-directed pill-taking population”.

articles.title: This $6 Tool Makes Peeling Garlic Extremely Easy
articles.summary: Plus, no more garlic-scented fingers for days.
body: Garlic is infamously annoying to peel. The fresher the cloves, the tighter their skin. (And, inevitably, the more your fingernails will smell like garlic post-peel.) I used to see a recipe that called for more than four cloves and feel my heart rate go up. Then one day, my life changed. My mother gifted me a little silicone tube. “It’s a garlic peeler!” she exclaimed.

I mentally rolled my eyes at the idea of a unitasker, which would only take up precious drawer space. I figured it would be just like herb scissors, an avocado slicer, or a quesadilla-maker—clickbait gadgets that are objectively unnecessary when kitchen shears, paring knives, and cast-iron skillets already exist.

Quite frankly, I forgot about the garlic peeler for a long time. Then, a recipe for toum caught my eye: I needed to peel 8 cloves. Ugh. And then I remembered that little tube. Let’s give it a try. I popped in a couple cloves, rolled it back and forth a few times, then dumped out the naked garlic, plus papery skins. Eureka!

articles.title: Soy-Marinated Eggs and More Recipes We Made This Week
articles.summary: Like kimchi tuna melts and a potato chip tower.
body: It’s no secret that Bon Appétit editors cook a lot for work. So it should come as no surprise that we cook a lot during our off hours too. Here are the recipes we’re whipping up this month to get dinner on the table, entertain our friends, satisfy a sweet tooth, use up leftovers, and everything in between. For even more staff favorites, click here.

For Bon Appétit’s inaugural Pantry Awards, our team tasted hundreds of products in the Test Kitchen: new snacks, sauces, drinks, and more. (An honest day’s work.) Since then, our editors have been using the winning pantry items in their own kitchens, folding them into weeknight dinners, delightful noshes, and chic cocktails. Here’s how.

Leave it to my colleague Hana Asbrink to make classic shrimp scampi even better. Her riff with chewy udon and an ultra-buttery, umami-packed sauce is the only way I want to eat it from now on. I used Potluck Doenjang, a winner from our Pantry Awards that’s thoughtfully made and intensely flavorful. Once the noodles were gone (cry), we used steamed broccoli to sop up every last drop. — E.L.
In her column, Good for You, Rebecca Firkser shares healthy recipes that are also extremely delicious.
